text:
elaine: proposal — move a small amount of trace aggregation into the obs-gateway to reduce downstream ingest costs and normalize span attributes. sketch: aggregate short lived spans (db row/kv ops) into a single 'micro-batch' span at the gateway, keep parent_id mapping, and attach a compressed payload for debug mode. :thinking:

sam: hmm. could save $ on es/trace retention, but we risk losing timing fidelity for root-caused latencies. how do we guarantee we can rehydrate if needed?

raj: rehydrate only possible if we keep raw payloads for a short window and a pointer to full snapshot stored in cold storage. tradeoff: storage vs query cost. also cardinality: need to strip high-card tags before aggregation.

elaine: agree. suggested constraints: 1) only aggregate spans <25ms and repeated >N times in 1s window, 2) drop user-specific tags (email, request_id) unless flagged, 3) store detailed blobs for 1h then cold archive for 30d.

sam: how do we express this in the schema? we need a versioned field so downstream consumers know it's aggregated. e.g. add span.attribute: "rw.redwood.agg_v" and a "rw.redwood.agg_summary" object. consumers must ignore by default if unknown.

morgan: prefer minimal surface area. what if we instead emit synthetic metric counters at gateway (counts, p50/p95) and keep traces untouched? metrics are cheaper but we lose causal span edges.

taylor: metrics-only loses causal graph — harder for SRE to debug cascading failures. gateway aggregation can keep parent-child topology by emitting a synthetic 'batch span' with children_count and approximate durations. example payload: 

```
{
  "span_id": "4f2a...",
  "trace_id": "9a7b...",
  "name": "db.micro_batch",
  "attributes": {
    "rw.redwood.agg_v": "v1",
    "rw.redwood.children_count": "18",
    "rw.redwood.dur_ms_p50": "2",
    "rw.redwood.dur_ms_p95": "6",
    "rw.redwood.sample_mode": "aggregated",
    "rw.redwood.detail_ptr": "s3://obs-aux/trace/1961234567/4f2a..."
  }
}
```

elaine: exactly. plus keep a small hashed fingerprint of the original spans for de-dup and quick-match.

raj: rollout concerns: clients and downstream consumers read raw spans today. need graceful schema evolution: implement gateway feature flag + release consumer-side parser that tolerates unknown attributes. plan: canary gateway -> ship parser shim (reads agg_v) -> flip flag for non-prod -> monitor errors.

sam: also watch cardinality explosion from resource.tags. we should attach a whitelist/blacklist on the gateway config and enforce normalize_keys (kebab-case) + value bucketing for common numeric tags.

morgan: ops and billing: how do we attribute cost per-customer if we aggregate across multi-tenant gateway? must preserve billing keys on batch spans or propagate a per-span billing token. can't drop that.

elaine: agreed. mandatory: keep billing_key at top-level of batch span (rw.billing.key) and make it required for dedicated tenants; for hosted we fallback to sticky route key.

taylor: testing checklist proposal: 
- unit tests for aggregator logic (edge cases: partial parent, orphan spans)
- compatibility tests for downstream consumers (ingest, trace UI, eval jobs)
- perf test: gateway CPU and memory under 1k req/s
- e2e: canary in staging for 48h with full debug logging enabled for 1% of traffic

gazebo-bot: deploybot: created canary target 'obs-gateway/agg-v1' in staging (canary id: cg-1961234). :white_check_mark: 

raj: timeline idea: two-week spike to build aggregator + schema shim, then 1 week canary, then opt-in for dedicated tenants, then onboard hosted slowly.

sam: one more: ensure the sampling/explainability story — a dashboard showing how many spans are aggregated vs raw, per-service, per-tenant. without that ops will be blind.

elaine: yep — telemetry and alerting first. I'll write a short RFC with the options and the rollout steps. tagging @taylor @raj for review. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: note: RFC draft created — /docs/rfcs/obs/gateway-aggregation-v1.md (draft).

morgan: thanks all — looks actionable. I'll sync with billing team about per-tenant keys.

sam: thanks. leaving comments on the RFC now.
